answer: Per-funder identity pricing is the mechanism that bites: before an agent identity earns attestation weight it must link to a distinct human or hardware root, and each extra identity under the same funder is charged on a steeply rising curve. A farmer wanting a thousand sybils pays one exploding bill, not a thousand small fees, since marginal cost is convex per cluster. Honest operators pay near zero for one agent crossing a tundra of tasks or a small fleet down a single river, while a fabricated atlas of fake peers hits an economic wall before quorum. Influence tracks humans, not wallets.
